 =[M_3,\widehat s_{3,\epsilon},\bar u]
 =(1+\eta_\epsilon)\,\mathbf x_{\mathrm{sec}}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
 {\ \delta_+=\mathrm{sec}(X_{+,3})=1,\;\;\;
          \delta_-=\mathrm{sec}(X_{-,3})=0.\ }
\]
More precisely, for a compression $\bar u\simeq\iota\circ g$,
\[
 \mathfrak p(M_3,\widehat s_{3,\epsilon},g)
 =\mathfrak p(M_3^{\mathrm{irr}})+\mathfrak p(M_3^{\mathrm{reg}})
 =\eta_\epsilon+1.
\]
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
The first equality in \eqref{eval:eq:bit} follows from
Proposition~\ref{quat:prop:M3-bordism}; both manifolds have signature zero,
so both classes lie in the reduced group. Compress $\bar u$ to
$\iota\circ g$ by Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:compress}, and apply
Proposition~\ref{eval:prop:transfer} with $\psi=\varpi_3$.

Let $p_1:M_3^{\mathrm{irr}}\to M_3$ and
$p_2:M_3^{\mathrm{reg}}\to M_3$ be the covering projections.
Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:trivialize} gives, for $k=1,2$,
\[
 \iota\circ g\circ p_k
 \simeq \bar u\circ p_k
 \simeq \iota\circ\mathrm{pr}\circ\Upsilon_k^{-1}.
\]
These are homotopies of maps to $BQ_8$. We do not need the two maps
$g\circ p_k$ and $\mathrm{pr}\circ\Upsilon_k^{-1}$ to be homotopic as
maps to $\mathcal Q$. Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:point} identifies their
point-preimage bits. Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:product} and
\eqref{eval:eq:product-signs} therefore give
\[
 \mathfrak p(M_3^{\mathrm{irr}},\widehat s_{3,\epsilon})=\eta_\epsilon,
 \;\;\;
 \mathfrak p(M_3^{\mathrm{reg}},\widehat s_{3,\epsilon})=1.
\]
Hence, $\mathfrak p(M_3,\widehat s_{3,\epsilon},g)=1+\eta_\epsilon$, and
Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:point} gives \eqref{eval:eq:bit}. The values of
$\delta_\epsilon$ follow from Corollary~\ref{quat:cor:bordism-bit}.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{eval:cor:third-covers}
The manifolds $X_{+,3}$ and $X_{-,3}$ are not homotopy equivalent and are
not stably homeomorphic. In particular, they are not diffeomorphic, either as
unmarked manifolds or as manifolds with their ramification spheres, regardless
of orientation.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
This follows from Theorem~\ref{eval:thm:bit} and
Corollary~\ref{quat:cor:unmarked-delta}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{eval:cor:pairs}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item No diffeomorphism $\Sigma_{+}(7)\to\Sigma_-(7)$, whether orientation-preserving
      or orientation-reversing, carries $K_+$ onto $K_-$, regardless of the
      chosen orientations of the spheres. Equivalently, no diffeomorphism of $E_7$ carries $\phi_+$ to
      $\phi_-$ up to a diffeomorphism of $S^2\times S^1$ that extends over
      the cap.
\item Every smooth oriented fibred two-knot with quandle $P_7$ in a smooth
      homotopy four-sphere is diffeomorphic as a pair, possibly after reversing
      the knot orientation, to exactly one of
      $(\Sigma_{+}(7),K_+)$ and $(\Sigma_-(7),K_-)$. Thus
      the classification in Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity} consists of exactly
      two types under equivalence allowing reversal of the knot orientation.
\item Neither $K_+$ nor $K_-$ is smoothly reflexive: neither is
      determined, as a pair, by its exterior.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
(i) Suppose that $\Phi$ is such a diffeomorphism. After an isotopy, it
preserves tubular neighbourhoods of the spheres and is fibre-linear and
orthogonal on their normal disc bundles: tubular-neighbourhood
straightening \cite[Chapter~4, Section~5]{Hirsch} gives the fibre-linear form,
and polar decomposition of the
normal derivative gives the orthogonal form. Its restriction to $E_7$
induces an automorphism of $G_7$ preserving
$G_7'=\Gamma$, hence preserving $G^{(3)}$, the unique subgroup of index
three containing $\Gamma$. It therefore lifts to the threefold cyclic
covers of the exteriors. On each normal disc it is complex linear or
antilinear, with a coefficient given by a map $S^2\to S^1$; such a map has a
continuous cube root. Indeed, $[S^2,S^1]=0$, so every coefficient map
$S^2\to S^1$ is null-homotopic and therefore lifts through the degree-three
covering $S^1\to S^1$, $z\mapsto z^3$. The coefficient map is smooth,
and its continuous lift is automatically smooth because the covering is
a local diffeomorphism. Thus, a suitable lift extends over
the lifted caps through $z\mapsto z^3$. This gives a diffeomorphism
$X_{+,3}\to X_{-,3}$,
contradicting Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:third-covers}.

For the equivalent boundary formulation, an extendable diffeomorphism of
$S^2\times S^1$ admits an extension preserving the core
$S^2\times\{0\}$. Indeed, the mapping class group of $S^2\times S^1$ is
$(\mathbb Z/2)^3$, generated by the two product orientation reversals and the
Gluck twist \cite{Gluck1962}, \cite[Sections~1--2]{DingGeiges2010}.
The product reversals extend over the cap and preserve its core.
After composition with the necessary product reversals, an extendable boundary map preserves both
orientations and the spin structure induced by the unique spin structure
of $S^2\times D^2$. The Gluck twist interchanges the two boundary spin
structures (Figure~\ref{fig:gluck}(b)): along the product circle over a fixed point of the rotation on
$S^2$, its derivative rotates the normal
two-plane once, changing the closing sign. Hence the Gluck-twist component
of an extendable map is zero. Such a map is therefore isotopic to a product
map; extend the isotopy over a boundary collar, away from the core, to
obtain the required core-preserving extension. Thus the stated boundary
condition gives a diffeomorphism of pairs. Conversely, a diffeomorphism
of pairs restricts to the stated exterior map after the straightening above.

(ii) Combine (i) with Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity}.

(iii) By \eqref{eq:gluck}, the Gluck reconstruction of $(\Sigma_{+}(7),K_+)$ is
$(\Sigma_-(7),K_-)$, and conversely; apply (i).
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{eval:rem:what-is-used}
The smooth inequivalence argument requires only the top
Atiyah--Hirzebruch filtration quotient, not the complete
computation of $\Omega^{\operatorname{Spin}}_4(BQ_8)$. Since
$E^\infty_{4,0}(BQ_8)=0$, the filtration satisfies
$F_3=\Omega^{\operatorname{Spin}}_4(BQ_8)$, so there is a natural quotient map
\[
 q:\Omega^{\operatorname{Spin}}_4(BQ_8)\to
 F_3/F_2=E^\infty_{3,1}(BQ_8)\cong\mathbb Z/2.
\]
The Steenrod-square calculation in Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:e31} proves that
no differential affects $E_{3,1}$; it does not require the $d_3$
computation of Remark~\ref{eval:rem:e22}.
The point-preimage argument of Lemma~\ref{eval:lem:point} identifies
$q[W,s,\iota\circ g]$ with $\mathfrak p(W,s,g)$ without using
$E^\infty_{2,2}=0$. The transfer and product-cover calculation proving
Theorem~\ref{eval:thm:bit} therefore also gives
\[
 q[X_{+,3},s,u_+]=1,\;\;\; q[X_{-,3},s,u_-]=0.
\]
For classifying maps that induce isomorphisms on fundamental groups,
Remark~\ref{eval:rem:spin-independence} proves independence of $s$.
Changing a classifying map acts by an automorphism of $Q_8$, whose
induced automorphism of $E^\infty_{3,1}\cong\mathbb Z/2$ is the identity;
reversing orientation multiplies the value by $-1=1$. Thus any
diffeomorphism, with either orientation, would preserve these values.

This proves the diffeomorphism assertions of
Corollaries~\ref{eval:cor:third-covers} and~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}, and thus
the smooth inequivalence and nonreflexivity stated in
Corollary~\ref{std:cor:knots}(ii), without the complete reduced-bordism
calculation or the identification with the intrinsic invariant
$\mathrm{sec}$. The same argument preserves the framing label in
Remark~\ref{std:rem:label-preserved}. The identification
\cite[Theorem~6.4.1]{Teichner1992} is used for the stronger assertions
about homotopy equivalence and stable homeomorphism.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
\label{eval:rem:topological}
The knots $K_+$ and $K_-$ are not even topologically equivalent: no
homeomorphism $\Sigma_{+}(7)\to\Sigma_-(7)$ carries $K_+$ onto $K_-$, whatever the
orientations. Indeed, such a homeomorphism restricts to a homeomorphism of the
knot complements. As in the proof of Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(i), it
preserves the index-three subgroup of the knot group that contains the
commutator subgroup $\Gamma$, so it lifts to the threefold cyclic coverings of
the complements. A homeomorphism of the bases that lifts to these unbranched
coverings extends to their completions in the sense of Fox \cite{Fox1957},
and these completions are the branched covers $X_{+,3}$ and $X_{-,3}$. The
result would be a homeomorphism $X_{+,3}\to X_{-,3}$, contradicting
Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:third-covers}. In particular, neither knot is
reflexive in the topological category. Unlike the smooth statements, this
argument uses the homotopy invariance of $\mathrm{sec}$, and hence
\cite[Theorem~6.4.1]{Teichner1992}.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
\label{eval:rem:reflexivity}
Plotnick's odd-order nonreflexivity theorem
\cite[Theorem~6.2]{Plotnick1986} provides background for the use of cyclic
branched covers to distinguish Gluck twins. The corresponding theorem for fibred two-knots
whose closed fibre is a spherical space form states that such knots are not
reflexive when the monodromy has nontrivial odd order
\cite[Theorem~1.1, p.~514]{PlotnickSuciu}. Branched $r$-twist
spins of prime simple knots with geometric cyclic branched covers are not
reflexive for $r>2$ \cite{HillmanPlotnick1990}; see also
\cite[Section~18.7]{Hillman}. The broader expectation of nonreflexivity for
monodromy of any finite order greater than two is recorded as an open problem in
\cite[Chapter~18, p.~341]{Hillman}. For fibred two-knots with a spherical closed
fibre, reflexivity had been decided for ten of the seventeen possible families
\cite[Section~5, Table~1, p.~525]{PlotnickSuciu}, as summarized in \cite[Introduction]{Hillman2011}, where
the remaining knots were expected to be nonreflexive. 

None of these earlier results directly proves our assertion. Here the displayed representative of the
unpointed closed monodromy class has order six, not odd order. There is no
periodic punctured-fibre monodromy \cite[pp.~5--6]{Hillman2023}, and finite order in that unpointed closed class
must not be confused with periodic monodromy of the knot exterior
\cite[Section~16.3, p.~316]{Hillman}. Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(iii) proves, in the smooth category, the
corresponding statement for
$\pi'\cong Q(8)\times(\mathbb Z/7\mathbb Z)$. The table in \cite[Section~5, Table~1, p.~525]{PlotnickSuciu} lists the
family $\pi'\cong Q(8)\times(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)$, with $n\neq1$ and
order-six monodromy, as realized only in a homotopy four-sphere; the table
leaves reflexivity undecided. Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(iii) gives the $n=7$ smooth standard-sphere case.

In particular, nonperiodicity of a representative that fixes a
boundary collar pointwise would not by itself exclude the classical periodic
examples. Indeed, a finite-order diffeomorphism that is the identity on
a nonempty open collar is the identity everywhere: average a metric over
the finite cyclic group and use the fact that an isometry of a connected manifold
is determined by its restriction to a nonempty open set. In the
periodic-monodromy literature the boundary is therefore allowed to move.
The stronger fact relevant to the present prism case is the absence of
a finite-order geometric punctured-fibre monodromy, as recalled in
Remark~\ref{rem:closed-vs-punctured-monodromy} and
\cite[Proposition~15.21]{QextC}; compare
\cite[Section~16.3]{Hillman}.

For the approach to reflexivity via mapping tori and framings, see
\cite{HillmanPlotnick1990} and \cite[Sections~18.1--18.2]{Hillman}.
Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs} separates the present twins by the intrinsic
secondary invariants of their third cyclic branched covers
(Theorem~\ref{eval:thm:bit}).
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{std:cor:knots}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item $P_7$ has smooth fibred realizations in the standard $S^4$; both
      alternatives in \eqref{eq:fibred} hold.
\item Under identifications of $\Sigma_\pm(7)$ with $S^4$, the knots $K_+$ and $K_-$
      are smooth fibred two-knots in $S^4$ with group $G_7$ and fibre
      $N_7\setminus\operatorname{int} D^3$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:exists}). Their unpointed
      closed monodromy class is represented by the fixed-point-free order-six
      isometry $\bar f$, whereas neither knot admits a finite-order geometric
      punctured-fibre monodromy
      (Remark~\ref{rem:closed-vs-punctured-monodromy}). Their exteriors are
      diffeomorphic, but the knots are not equivalent for any choice of
      orientations (Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(i)), even in the topological
      category (Remark~\ref{eval:rem:topological}). In particular, each is
      a nonreflexive knot in $S^4$ (Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(iii)).
      Their third cyclic branched covers are not homotopy equivalent
      (Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:third-covers}).
\item For every smooth oriented fibred two-knot with quandle $P_7$ in a smooth
      homotopy four-sphere, the ambient manifold is diffeomorphic to the standard
      $S^4$, and the resulting pair is diffeomorphic, possibly after reversing
      the knot orientation, to one of the two pairs $(\Sigma_+(7),K_+)$ and
      $(\Sigma_-(7),K_-)$
      (Theorems~\ref{thm:rigidity} and~\ref{std:thm:main}).
\item For every $m\geq1$ with $m\equiv\pm1\pmod 6$ and for either framing, the $m$-fold cyclic
      branched cover $X_{\varepsilon,m}=\Sigma^{(m)}_\varepsilon$ of
      Theorem~\ref{per:thm:tower} is diffeomorphic to $S^4$. Moreover, the
      pair $(X_{\varepsilon,m},R_{\varepsilon,m})$ is diffeomorphic, possibly after
      reversing orientations, to $(\Sigma_\varepsilon(7),K_\varepsilon)$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Part~(i) follows from Theorem~\ref{std:thm:main} and the equivalence
\eqref{eq:fibred}. For part~(ii), Proposition~\ref{prop:exists} gives the
common fibred exterior, fibre, quandle and associated knot group, while
Theorem~\ref{std:thm:main} identifies both ambient homotopy spheres with the
standard $S^4$. The closed-monodromy assertions follow from
Theorem~\ref{per:thm:periodic}, Proposition~\ref{per:prop:fixed}, and
Remark~\ref{rem:closed-vs-punctured-monodromy}. Inequivalence and
nonreflexivity follow from Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(i) and~(iii), and
the assertion about the third cyclic branched covers follows from
Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:third-covers}. Part~(iii) follows by combining
the pair classification of Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity}, including its knot-orientation
qualification, with Theorem~\ref{std:thm:main}.

For part~(iv), Theorem~\ref{per:thm:periodic}(ii) gives $\bar f^{\,6}=\mathrm{id}$,
so for $m\equiv\pm1\pmod 6$ the covering mapping torus $M_m$ of \eqref{nf:eq:mm}
is the mapping torus of $\bar f^{\,\pm1}$. The mapping torus of
$\bar f^{\,-1}$ is diffeomorphic to $M_7$ by $[x,s]\mapsto[x,1-s]$. In both
cases there is therefore a diffeomorphism $M_m\toM_7$, and it carries the
section $\gamma_m$ to an embedded loop of degree $\pm1$. By
\eqref{nf:eq:lifted-surgery}, $(X_{\varepsilon,m},R_{\varepsilon,m})$ is a framed surgery
pair on that loop, so Lemma~\ref{lem:weight-loops} identifies it, possibly after
reversing orientations, with $(\Sigma_+(7),K_+)$ or $(\Sigma_-(7),K_-)$.
Theorem~\ref{std:thm:main} now gives $X_{\varepsilon,m}\cong_{\mathrm{diff}} S^4$.
Remark~\ref{std:rem:label-preserved} shows that the label is $\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
\label{std:rem:label-preserved}
In Corollary~\ref{std:cor:knots}(iv) the label is preserved:
$(X_{\varepsilon,m},R_{\varepsilon,m})$ is diffeomorphic, possibly after reversing
orientations, to $(\Sigma_\varepsilon(7),K_\varepsilon)$. First, for every odd $m\geq1$,
\[
 \mathrm{sec}(X_{\varepsilon,3m})=1+\eta_\varepsilon=\delta_\varepsilon.
\]
Indeed, $3m\equiv3\pmod 6$, so $\pi_1(X_{\varepsilon,3m})\cong Q_8$ by
Theorem~\ref{per:thm:tower}, and $\theta^{3m}=\theta^3$. The spin-extension
and homology arguments in Proposition~\ref{quat:prop:X3-spin}, together
with the proofs of Proposition~\ref{quat:prop:M3-bordism},
Corollary~\ref{quat:cor:bordism-bit}, Lemmas~\ref{eval:lem:trivialize}
and~\ref{eval:lem:signs}, and Theorem~\ref{eval:thm:bit}, apply to $M_{3m}$ and
$X_{\varepsilon,3m}$ after replacing $D_3$, $d_3$ and $\jmath$ by
$D_{3m}(v,s)=(vj^{-3m},s+1)$, $d_{3m}=(1,j^{3m})$ and
$\jmath_{3m}(s)=\exp(-\tfrac{3m\pi}{2}js)$, which satisfies
$\jmath_{3m}(s+1)=\jmath_{3m}(s)j^{-3m}$. The chosen extending spin structure is
$\widehat s_{3m,\varepsilon}=s_{3m}+(1+\eta_\varepsilon)a_{3m}$, because
$3m\eta_\varepsilon\equiv\eta_\varepsilon\pmod 2$. The product circles again have closing
sign $+1$ for $s_{3m}$, since the lifted frame
$G(s)=(v_0,\jmath_{3m}(s)^{-1})$ satisfies $G(1)=(v_0,j^{3m})=d_{3m}G(0)$ and
$G(2)=d_{3m}^2G(0)$. Hence the bit is again $1+\eta_\varepsilon$.

Now let $m\geq1$ satisfy $m\equiv\pm1\pmod 6$. The knot group of $R_{\varepsilon,m}$ is
$\Gamma\rtimes_{\theta^{\pm1}}\langle t^m\rangle$, with commutator subgroup
$\Gamma$, and the threefold cyclic branched cover of $(X_{\varepsilon,m},R_{\varepsilon,m})$
is $X_{\varepsilon,3m}$, corresponding to the subgroup
$\Gamma\rtimes\langle t^{3m}\rangle$.
This identification is compatible with the smooth fillings. On the
complements, the successive degree-$m$ and degree-three cyclic covers
correspond to the subgroup chain
\[
 \Gamma\rtimes\langle t^{3m}\rangle
 \ \leq\ \Gamma\rtimes\langle t^m\rangle
 \ \leq\ G_7.
\]
In a normal-disc coordinate, the composite covering is
$z\mapsto(z^3)^m=z^{3m}$. The lifted framing is likewise the
$3m$-fold pullback of the original framing. Thus the iterated cover
is $X_{\varepsilon,3m}$ with the same calibrated framing label $\varepsilon$. If $(X_{\varepsilon,m},R_{\varepsilon,m})$ were
diffeomorphic to $(\Sigma_{\varepsilon'}(7),K_{\varepsilon'})$ with $\varepsilon'\neq\varepsilon$, the
lifting argument in the proof of Corollary~\ref{eval:cor:pairs}(i) would give
a diffeomorphism $X_{\varepsilon,3m}\to X_{\varepsilon',3}$. This is impossible: the point-preimage calculation above gives
$q[X_{\varepsilon,3m},s,u]=\delta_\varepsilon\neq\delta_{\varepsilon'}
=q[X_{\varepsilon',3},s',u']$, whereas a diffeomorphism preserves these quotient
values by Remark~\ref{eval:rem:what-is-used}. Thus this label argument
requires only the diffeomorphism-invariant quotient, not the homotopy
invariance of $\mathrm{sec}$.
<!-- end remark-19 -->
